problem: Glass had not reached a consumer-ready state and faced public concern.
title: Google ends consumer sales of Glass and moves the project out of Google X
context: Google sold Glass to early adopters through its Explorer programme at $1,500, and the camera drew privacy criticism.
decision_made: End the Explorer programme on 19 January 2015 and reorganise Glass as a stand-alone division.
action_taken: Said it would keep supplying companies and developers and expected a new version later.
observed_outcome: Direct consumer sales ended and Glass never moved beyond beta to retail sale, according to later reporting.
observation_period: About 2 years from launch of the programme
lessons: A product that raises privacy concerns and has unclear everyday value can struggle even with strong brand and attention.
limitations: The phrase "Glass hole" was not found in the sources used. Later enterprise versions were not checked here.

claims.claim_text: Google ended the Glass Explorer programme, which sold the beta version at $1,500, from 19 January 2015.
eWeek reported that Glass remained in beta testing and never reached retail sale to consumers.
